title: Index Energy Line Corrections for the Pass-Through Cycle - C&I
content:
## Correcting the index energy line of the pass-through cycle (Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts)

An index line correction returns what the index energy charge line of the pass-through cycle was billed above the index price the contract allows, the pass-through cycle being the cycle that began on the stated effective date of the contract's latest regulatory pass-through notice; it is posted, when the business disputes the line, as one rebill credit tied to that line through its reference number, and only when the over-billed amount is positive.

The latest regulatory pass-through notice is the one with the latest notice date among the contract's notices.

## Posting the credit: `credit_index_line_725777e6`

The agent unlocks `credit_index_line_725777e6` and then calls it.

**Capability.** One call posts a rebill credit against one index energy bill line of a commercial and industrial electricity contract that the business disputes as billed above the index price its contract allows. It adds one rebill credit line, dated today, to the same contract's bill, tied to the disputed line and dated to that line's billing cycle; the net charges billed on the contract fall by the credited amount, and the credit then appears among the contract's bill lines. The disputed line itself is not changed.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `source_billing_id` | the reference number of the disputed index energy bill line, as shown on the bill lines returned by the C&I bill lookup | bill line reference |
| `amount_usd` | the rebill credit | US dollars, a negative number rounded half up to 2 decimal places; stored exactly as passed |

**Return.** A confirmation carrying `cni_billing_id` (the reference number of the new rebill credit line), `source_billing_id` (the line corrected), `cni_contract_id` (the contract credited), `line_type`, always `rebill_credit`, `billing_period_start` (the corrected line's cycle, YYYY-MM-DD), `amount_usd` (negative, 2 decimal places) and `posted_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD).
